claim: Lung epithelial progenitors differentiate into alveolar type 1 (AT1) and type 2 (AT2) cells.
source: Lung epithelial progenitors differentiate into alveolar type 1 (AT1) and type 2 (AT2) cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge about lung development.

claim: AT1 cells form the air-blood interface.
source: These cells form the air-blood interface and secrete surfactant, respectively, and are essential for lung maturation and function.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about AT1 cell function.

claim: AT2 cells secrete surfactant.
source: These cells form the air-blood interface and secrete surfactant, respectively, and are essential for lung maturation and function.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about AT2 cell function.

claim: AT1 and AT2 cells are essential for lung maturation and function.
source: These cells form the air-blood interface and secrete surfactant, respectively, and are essential for lung maturation and function.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about alveolar cell importance.

claim: Current protocols to derive and culture alveolar cells do not faithfully recapitulate the architecture of the distal lung.
source: Current protocols to derive and culture alveolar cells do not faithfully recapitulate the architecture of the distal lung, which influences cell fate patterns in vivo.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of existing methods, based on the authors' assessment of the literature.

claim: Distal lung architecture influences cell fate patterns in vivo.
source: Current protocols to derive and culture alveolar cells do not faithfully recapitulate the architecture of the distal lung, which influences cell fate patterns in vivo.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the role of tissue architecture.

claim: Serum-free conditions allow for growth and differentiation of mouse distal lung epithelial progenitors.
source: Here, we report serum-free conditions that allow for growth and differentiation of mouse distal lung epithelial progenitors.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by the experimental data presented.

claim: Collagen I promotes the differentiation of flattened, polarized AT1 cells.
source: We find that Collagen I promotes the differentiation of flattened, polarized AT1 cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Casein Kinase activity is associated with maintenance of an AT2 expression signature.
source: We identify an association between Casein Kinase activity and maintenance of an AT2 expression signature; Casein Kinase inhibition leads to an increase in AT1/progenitor cell ratio.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the chemical screen and subsequent analysis.

claim: Casein Kinase inhibition leads to an increase in AT1/progenitor cell ratio.
source: We identify an association between Casein Kinase activity and maintenance of an AT2 expression signature; Casein Kinase inhibition leads to an increase in AT1/progenitor cell ratio.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by data in Figure 3C.

claim: Lung alveolar progenitor cells differentiate at saccular stages (E17 in mouse, 26 weeks in human).
source: Lung alveolar progenitor cells differentiate at saccular stages (E17 in mouse, 26 weeks in human) into flattened alveolar type 1 (AT1) cells, constituting the surface for gas exchange, and secretory type 2 (AT2) cells, which prevent alveolar collapse by secreting pulmonary surfactant (Morrisey and Hogan, 2010; Chao et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: AT1 cells constitute the surface for gas exchange.
source: Lung alveolar progenitor cells differentiate at saccular stages (E17 in mouse, 26 weeks in human) into flattened alveolar type 1 (AT1) cells, constituting the surface for gas exchange, and secretory type 2 (AT2) cells, which prevent alveolar collapse by secreting pulmonary surfactant (Morrisey and Hogan, 2010; Chao et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: AT2 cells prevent alveolar collapse by secreting pulmonary surfactant.
source: Lung alveolar progenitor cells differentiate at saccular stages (E17 in mouse, 26 weeks in human) into flattened alveolar type 1 (AT1) cells, constituting the surface for gas exchange, and secretory type 2 (AT2) cells, which prevent alveolar collapse by secreting pulmonary surfactant (Morrisey and Hogan, 2010; Chao et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Fetal distal lung progenitors are thought to be bipotent.
source: Fetal distal lung progenitors are thought to be bipotent and they co-express markers of both AT1 and AT2 cells, including Podoplanin/PDPN and Advanced Glycosylation End product-specific Receptor/RAGE as well as Prosurfactant Protein C/SFTPC, respectively (Desai et al., 2014; Treutlein et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Fetal distal lung progenitors co-express markers of both AT1 and AT2 cells, including Podoplanin/PDPN and Advanced Glycosylation End product-specific Receptor/RAGE as well as Prosurfactant Protein C/SFTPC.
source: Fetal distal lung progenitors are thought to be bipotent and they co-express markers of both AT1 and AT2 cells, including Podoplanin/PDPN and Advanced Glycosylation End product-specific Receptor/RAGE as well as Prosurfactant Protein C/SFTPC, respectively (Desai et al., 2014; Treutlein et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Differentiation of progenitors into AT1 and AT2 cells is regulated by multiple signals including WNT and FGF from the mesenchyme.
source: Differentiation of progenitors into AT1 and AT2 cells is regulated by multiple signals including WNT (Wingless and Int-1) and FGF (Fibroblast Growth Factor) from the mesenchyme (Volckaert and De Langhe, 2015; Li et al., 2018), mechanical forces (Li et al., 2018), epigenetic modifications (Wang et al., 2016), and the extracellular matrix (ECM) (Kim et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Differentiation of progenitors into AT1 and AT2 cells is regulated by mechanical forces.
source: Differentiation of progenitors into AT1 and AT2 cells is regulated by multiple signals including WNT (Wingless and Int-1) and FGF (Fibroblast Growth Factor) from the mesenchyme (Volckaert and De Langhe, 2015; Li et al., 2018), mechanical forces (Li et al., 2018), epigenetic modifications (Wang et al., 2016), and the extracellular matrix (ECM) (Kim et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Differentiation of progenitors into AT1 and AT2 cells is regulated by epigenetic modifications.

evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Differentiation of progenitors into AT1 and AT2 cells is regulated by the extracellular matrix (ECM).

evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: WNT signaling promotes the expansion of Axin2+ AT2 cells during alveologenesis.
source: In particular, WNT signaling was shown to promote the expansion of Axin2+ AT2 cells during alveologenesis and prevent their conversion to the AT1 lineage (Frank et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: WNT signaling prevents conversion of Axin2+ AT2 cells to the AT1 lineage.
source: In particular, WNT signaling was shown to promote the expansion of Axin2+ AT2 cells during alveologenesis and prevent their conversion to the AT1 lineage (Frank et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: WNT activity marks lung progenitors in homeostasis and regeneration.
source: Similarly, WNT activity marks lung progenitors in homeostasis and regeneration, and WNT inhibition leads to AT1 differentiation (Nabhan et al., 2018; Zacharias et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: WNT inhibition leads to AT1 differentiation.
source: Similarly, WNT activity marks lung progenitors in homeostasis and regeneration, and WNT inhibition leads to AT1 differentiation (Nabhan et al., 2018; Zacharias et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: β-catenin is required for the maintenance of distal lung progenitors during mouse fetal development.
source: During mouse fetal development, β-catenin is required for the maintenance of distal lung progenitors (Ostrin et al., 2018); however, a mechanistic understanding of how WNT signaling controls AT1/AT2 cell differentiation or fate selection is currently lacking (Aros et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: A mechanistic understanding of how WNT signaling controls AT1/AT2 cell differentiation or fate selection is currently lacking.
source: During mouse fetal development, β-catenin is required for the maintenance of distal lung progenitors (Ostrin et al., 2018); however, a mechanistic understanding of how WNT signaling controls AT1/AT2 cell differentiation or fate selection is currently lacking (Aros et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: 3D cultures of lung- or iPSC-derived alveolar progenitor cells have been used to model respiratory cell fate specification and signaling/cell interactions.
source: 3D cultures of lung- or iPSC-derived alveolar progenitor cells have been used to model respiratory cell fate specification and signaling/cell interactions (reviewed by Gkatzis et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a review article.

claim: Existing 3D culture models fail to recapitulate the defined epithelial architecture of the mouse lung at canalicular and saccular stages.
source: However, these models fail to recapitulate the defined epithelial architecture of the mouse lung at canalicular and saccular stages, with HOPX+ cells residing in the stalk and SOX9+/SFTPC+ cells in the tip region (Frank et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: In the mouse lung at canalicular and saccular stages, HOPX+ cells reside in the stalk and SOX9+/SFTPC+ cells in the tip region.
source: However, these models fail to recapitulate the defined epithelial architecture of the mouse lung at canalicular and saccular stages, with HOPX+ cells residing in the stalk and SOX9+/SFTPC+ cells in the tip region (Frank et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Most lung organoid models have displayed a spheroid or unpatterned morphology until recently.
source: Until recently (Vazquez‐Armendariz et al., 2020), most models have displayed a spheroid or unpatterned morphology, making it difficult to assess localized differentiation from progenitors to alveolar cells.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: AT1 cells play a central role in lung development.
source: In addition, despite the central role of AT1 cells in lung development (Zepp et al., 2021), AT1 cell isolation and generation in vitro have been longstanding obstacles, and the efficiency of AT1 cell generation in vitro, or the properties of the cells obtained in these cultures, have not been analyzed in detail, limiting the relevance of these models for cell differentiation studies.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: AT1 cell isolation and generation in vitro have been longstanding obstacles.
source: In addition, despite the central role of AT1 cells in lung development (Zepp et al., 2021), AT1 cell isolation and generation in vitro have been longstanding obstacles, and the efficiency of AT1 cell generation in vitro, or the properties of the cells obtained in these cultures, have not been analyzed in detail, limiting the relevance of these models for cell differentiation studies.
evidence: This is stated as a known limitation in the field.

claim: The efficiency of AT1 cell generation in vitro has not been analyzed in detail.
source: In addition, despite the central role of AT1 cells in lung development (Zepp et al., 2021), AT1 cell isolation and generation in vitro have been longstanding obstacles, and the efficiency of AT1 cell generation in vitro, or the properties of the cells obtained in these cultures, have not been analyzed in detail, limiting the relevance of these models for cell differentiation studies.
evidence: This is stated as a known limitation in the field.

claim: At E14.5, lung pseudoglandular development is almost complete in mouse.
source: At E14.5, lung pseudoglandular development is almost complete in mouse and NKX2.1+ alveolar progenitors become specified (Frank et al., 2019), while the distal SOX9+ epithelial domain begins to expand compared with the proximal airway (Alanis et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: At E14.5, NKX2.1+ alveolar progenitors become specified.
source: At E14.5, lung pseudoglandular development is almost complete in mouse and NKX2.1+ alveolar progenitors become specified (Frank et al., 2019), while the distal SOX9+ epithelial domain begins to expand compared with the proximal airway (Alanis et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: At E14.5, the distal SOX9+ epithelial domain begins to expand compared with the proximal airway.
source: At E14.5, lung pseudoglandular development is almost complete in mouse and NKX2.1+ alveolar progenitors become specified (Frank et al., 2019), while the distal SOX9+ epithelial domain begins to expand compared with the proximal airway (Alanis et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Treatment with FGF7 and FGF10 led to epithelial growth and lumenization over three days.
source: We tested combinations of these factors and observed that treatment with FGF7 and FGF10 led to epithelial growth and lumenization over three days without inducing hyperproliferation of residual mesenchymal cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, B.

claim: Treatment with FGF7 and FGF10 did not induce hyperproliferation of residual mesenchymal cells.
source: We tested combinations of these factors and observed that treatment with FGF7 and FGF10 led to epithelial growth and lumenization over three days without inducing hyperproliferation of residual mesenchymal cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, B.

claim: Cryopreserved epithelial tips can be expanded in culture and form organoids in FGF-supplemented medium.
source: We further found that cryopreserved epithelial tips could be expanded in culture and formed organoids in FGF-supplemented medium (52% efficiency compared with 75% using freshly dissociated tissue, Figure 1B), thereby allowing for more experimental flexibility.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Cryopreserved epithelial tips form organoids with 52% efficiency compared with 75% using freshly dissociated tissue.
source: We further found that cryopreserved epithelial tips could be expanded in culture and formed organoids in FGF-supplemented medium (52% efficiency compared with 75% using freshly dissociated tissue, Figure 1B), thereby allowing for more experimental flexibility.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: On day 1, the epithelial tips reorganized to form a closed system (cyst) and began a process of lumen expansion.
source: Morphologically, on day 1, the epithelial tips reorganized to form a closed system (cyst) and began a process of lumen expansion.
evidence: This is a primary observation from the study.

claim: On day 2, a single large lumen was observed, along with newly formed epithelial branches.
source: On day 2, a single large lumen was observed, along with newly formed epithelial branches.
evidence: This is a primary observation from the study.

claim: By day 6, many epithelial branches had extended into the surrounding matrix.
source: By day 6, many epithelial branches had extended into the surrounding matrix (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is a primary observation from the study, supported by Figure 1C.

claim: SOX9 is a transcription factor restricted to the distal progenitor population in mouse and human.
source: To determine the location and dynamics of progenitor cells in the organoid cultures, we assessed the expression of SOX9, a transcription factor restricted to the distal progenitor population in mouse and human (Rock et al., 2009; Alanis et al., 2014; Nikolić et al., 2017; Frank et al., 2019), and which is required for lung epithelial differentiation (Rockich et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: SOX9 is required for lung epithelial differentiation.
source: To determine the location and dynamics of progenitor cells in the organoid cultures, we assessed the expression of SOX9, a transcription factor restricted to the distal progenitor population in mouse and human (Rock et al., 2009; Alanis et al., 2014; Nikolić et al., 2017; Frank et al., 2019), and which is required for lung epithelial differentiation (Rockich et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: SOX9+ cells were prevalent in isolated structures on day 0.
source: SOX9+ cells were prevalent in isolated structures on day 0, and SOX9 expression was maintained throughout organoid lumenization until day 2.
evidence: This is a primary observation from the study.

claim: SOX9 expression was maintained throughout organoid lumenization until day 2.
source: SOX9+ cells were prevalent in isolated structures on day 0, and SOX9 expression was maintained throughout organoid lumenization until day 2.
evidence: This is a primary observation from the study.

claim: During lumenization, the majority of cells in the organoids were proliferating.
source: During this process, the majority of cells in the organoids were proliferating.
evidence: This is a primary observation from the study.

claim: By day 6, the tips of newly formed epithelial branches contained fewer SOX9+ cells.
source: By day 6, the tips of newly formed epithelial branches contained fewer SOX9+ cells and also fewer proliferating cells as assessed by KI67 immunostaining (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a primary observation from the study, supported by Figure 1D.

claim: By day 6, the tips of newly formed epithelial branches contained fewer proliferating cells as assessed by KI67 immunostaining.
source: By day 6, the tips of newly formed epithelial branches contained fewer SOX9+ cells and also fewer proliferating cells as assessed by KI67 immunostaining (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a primary observation from the study, supported by Figure 1D.

claim: The distal progenitor state is initially maintained in the 3D cultures.
source: These data indicate that the distal progenitor state is initially maintained in the 3D cultures.
evidence: This is an inference based on the SOX9 expression data.

claim: The distal epithelial markers Id2, Bmp4 and Etv5 displayed higher expression levels on day 0 compared to E13.5 distal epithelial tips.
source: The distal epithelial markers Id2, Bmp4 and Etv5 displayed higher expression levels on day 0, possibly reflecting the enrichment in distal characteristics or the endogenous activation of a distal developmental program between E13 and E14 (Frank et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a primary finding from RT-qPCR analysis.

claim: Sox2 showed variable expression on day 0, suggesting that a variable number of proximal epithelial cells was isolated in the different experiments.
source: A marker of the proximal epithelium, Sox2, showed variable expression on day 0, suggesting that a variable number of proximal epithelial cells was isolated in the different experiments.
evidence: This is an inference based on Sox2 expression data.

claim: Sox2 was downregulated by day 2.
source: Sox2 was downregulated by day 2, suggesting that FGF10-supplemented media selectively support distal epithelial progenitors, as described previously (Bellusci et al., 1997; Danopoulos et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a primary finding from RT-qPCR analysis.

claim: FGF10-supplemented media selectively support distal epithelial progenitors.
source: Sox2 was downregulated by day 2, suggesting that FGF10-supplemented media selectively support distal epithelial progenitors, as described previously (Bellusci et al., 1997; Danopoulos et al., 2019).
evidence: This is an inference based on Sox2 downregulation and supported by citations.

claim: Id2, Bmp4, and to a lesser extent Sox9, displayed upregulation by day 2.
source: Conversely, other markers of distal lung progenitors, such as Id2, Bmp4, and to a lesser extent Sox9, displayed upregulation by day 2, which may indicate expansion or conversion into distal progenitor cell identity.
evidence: This is a primary finding from RT-qPCR analysis.

claim: By day 6, all analyzed distal progenitor markers, as well as Sox2, were downregulated compared with E13.5 epithelial tips.
source: By day 6, all analyzed distal progenitor markers, as well as Sox2, were downregulated compared with E13.5 epithelial tips, suggesting that the distal progenitor cell identity is progressively lost during culture (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: This is a primary finding from RT-qPCR analysis, supported by Figure 1D and E.

claim: The distal progenitor cell identity is progressively lost during culture.
source: By day 6, all analyzed distal progenitor markers, as well as Sox2, were downregulated compared with E13.5 epithelial tips, suggesting that the distal progenitor cell identity is progressively lost during culture (Figure 1D and E).
evidence: This is an inference based on the downregulation of progenitor markers.

claim: On day 6, epithelial branches appear to be patterned in the proximo-distal axis.
source: Since on day 6 epithelial branches appear to be patterned in the proximo-distal axis, are morphologically elongated, and have lost most proliferative capacity, similar to distal lung epithelium at late gestation (Frank et al., 2019), we hypothesized that distal epithelial progenitors undergo differentiation in culture.
evidence: This is a primary observation from the study.

claim: On day 6, epithelial branches are morphologically elongated.
source: Since on day 6 epithelial branches appear to be patterned in the proximo-distal axis, are morphologically elongated, and have lost most proliferative capacity, similar to distal lung epithelium at late gestation (Frank et al., 2019), we hypothesized that distal epithelial progenitors undergo differentiation in culture.
evidence: This is a primary observation from the study.

claim: On day 6, epithelial branches have lost most proliferative capacity.
source: Since on day 6 epithelial branches appear to be patterned in the proximo-distal axis, are morphologically elongated, and have lost most proliferative capacity, similar to distal lung epithelium at late gestation (Frank et al., 2019), we hypothesized that distal epithelial progenitors undergo differentiation in culture.
evidence: This is a primary observation from the study.

claim: Distal lung epithelium at late gestation is patterned in the proximo-distal axis, morphologically elongated, and has lost most proliferative capacity.
source: Since on day 6 epithelial branches appear to be patterned in the proximo-distal axis, are morphologically elongated, and have lost most proliferative capacity, similar to distal lung epithelium at late gestation (Frank et al., 2019), we hypothesized that distal epithelial progenitors undergo differentiation in culture.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Low SFTPC and RAGE staining intensity was observed on days 0 and 1.
source: Low staining intensity was observed on days 0 and 1, indicating that within the first days of culture, the organoids are mainly composed of undifferentiated progenitors.
evidence: This is a primary observation from immunostaining experiments.

claim: Within the first days of culture, the organoids are mainly composed of undifferentiated progenitors.
source: Low staining intensity was observed on days 0 and 1, indicating that within the first days of culture, the organoids are mainly composed of undifferentiated progenitors.
evidence: This is an inference based on low SFTPC and RAGE staining.

claim: On day 2, SFTPC/RAGE were co-expressed in a majority of the cells.
source: On day 2, SFTPC/RAGE were co-expressed in a majority of the cells, similar to what is observed with alveolar bipotent progenitors (Desai et al., 2014; Treutlein et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a primary observation from immunostaining experiments.

claim: Alveolar bipotent progenitors co-express SFTPC and RAGE.
source: On day 2, SFTPC/RAGE were co-expressed in a majority of the cells, similar to what is observed with alveolar bipotent progenitors (Desai et al., 2014; Treutlein et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: By day 6, two cell populations emerged: SFTPC-/RAGE+ cells in the stalk region of the elongated branches, and SFTPC+/RAGE- cells in the tip region or at new sites of branching.
source: By day 6, two cell populations emerged: SFTPC-/RAGE+ cells in the stalk region of the elongated branches, and SFTPC+/RAGE- cells in the tip region or at new sites of branching.
evidence: This is a primary observation from immunostaining experiments.

claim: The tip domain comprises cells co-expressing SFTPC and RAGE, suggesting the maintenance of a bipotent progenitor (BP) population.
source: The tip domain also comprised cells co-expressing SFTPC and RAGE, suggesting the maintenance of a bipotent progenitor (BP) population (Treutlein et al., 2014; Figure 2A).
evidence: This is an inference based on immunostaining data and supported by a citation.

claim: On day 6, there are approximately equal numbers of AT1 and BP cells in epithelial branches.
source: Quantification of the differentiated and progenitor cells on day 6 revealed approximately equal numbers of AT1 and BP cells in epithelial branches while AT2 cells were less prevalent (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a primary finding from quantification of immunostaining data, shown in Figure 2B.

claim: On day 6, AT2 cells were less prevalent than AT1 and BP cells in epithelial branches.
source: Quantification of the differentiated and progenitor cells on day 6 revealed approximately equal numbers of AT1 and BP cells in epithelial branches while AT2 cells were less prevalent (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a primary finding from quantification of immunostaining data, shown in Figure 2B.

claim: In the absence of Collagen I, the organoids displayed a reduced number of AT1 cells in favor of BP cells.
source: In the absence of Collagen I, the organoids displayed a reduced number of AT1 cells in favor of BP cells, indicating that a collagenous matrix (at 1:1 or 1:3 Matrigel/Collagen I ratio) promotes the differentiation of AT1 cells in vitro (Figure 2B), consistent with the reported role of the ECM in alveolar epithelial differentiation (Kim et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a primary finding from quantification of immunostaining data, shown in Figure 2B.

claim: A collagenous matrix (at 1:1 or 1:3 Matrigel/Collagen I ratio) promotes the differentiation of AT1 cells in vitro.
source: In the absence of Collagen I, the organoids displayed a reduced number of AT1 cells in favor of BP cells, indicating that a collagenous matrix (at 1:1 or 1:3 Matrigel/Collagen I ratio) promotes the differentiation of AT1 cells in vitro (Figure 2B), consistent with the reported role of the ECM in alveolar epithelial differentiation (Kim et al., 2018).
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison of AT1 cell numbers with and without Collagen I.

claim: The ECM plays a role in alveolar epithelial differentiation.
source: In the absence of Collagen I, the organoids displayed a reduced number of AT1 cells in favor of BP cells, indicating that a collagenous matrix (at 1:1 or 1:3 Matrigel/Collagen I ratio) promotes the differentiation of AT1 cells in vitro (Figure 2B), consistent with the reported role of the ECM in alveolar epithelial differentiation (Kim et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The expression level of differentiated cell markers, including Sftpc, Ager, Aqp5, and Hopx, progressively increased until day 6.
source: The expression level of differentiated cell markers, including Sftpc, Ager, Aqp5, and Hopx, progressively increased until day 6, at which point they reached levels comparable with those observed in E18.5 distal lung tissue (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a primary finding from RT-qPCR analysis, shown in Figure 2C.

claim: By day 6, the expression levels of Sftpc, Ager, Aqp5, and Hopx reached levels comparable with those observed in E18.5 distal lung tissue.
source: The expression level of differentiated cell markers, including Sftpc, Ager, Aqp5, and Hopx, progressively increased until day 6, at which point they reached levels comparable with those observed in E18.5 distal lung tissue (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a primary finding from RT-qPCR analysis, shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Distal progenitors differentiate within six days of organoid culture.
source: These data indicate that distal progenitors differentiate within six days of organoid culture, offering a simple model of early alveolar formation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the expression data of differentiation markers.

claim: SFTPC-/RAGE+ cells displayed exclusive basolateral localization of RAGE.
source: By immunostaining, we found that SFTPC-/RAGE+ cells displayed exclusive basolateral localization of RAGE (Figure 2A and D) and apical localization of Podocalyxin (PODXL) (Figure 2D), similar to observations in intact lung tissue at E19 (Yang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a primary observation from immunostaining experiments, shown in Figure 2A and D.

claim: SFTPC-/RAGE+ cells displayed apical localization of Podocalyxin (PODXL).
source: By immunostaining, we found that SFTPC-/RAGE+ cells displayed exclusive basolateral localization of RAGE (Figure 2A and D) and apical localization of Podocalyxin (PODXL) (Figure 2D), similar to observations in intact lung tissue at E19 (Yang et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a primary observation from immunostaining experiments, shown in Figure 2D.

claim: In intact lung tissue at E19, RAGE is localized basolaterally and PODXL is localized apically.
source: By immunostaining, we found that SFTPC-/RAGE+ cells displayed exclusive basolateral localization of RAGE (Figure 2A and D) and apical localization of Podocalyxin (PODXL) (Figure 2D), similar to observations in intact lung tissue at E19 (Yang et al., 2016).

claim: SFTPC-/RAGE+ cells were marked by uniform plasma membrane expression of Podoplanin/T1alpha (PDPN).

source: Immunostaining for Zonula Occludens-1 (ZO-1), a marker of tight junctions, labeled intercellular adhesions at the luminal/apical surface (Figure 2D) as previously reported (Yang et al., 2016), suggesting that the epithelial branches form an intact cellular monolayer and display barrier function.
evidence: This is a primary observation from immunostaining experiments, shown in Figure 2D.

claim: ZO-1 labels intercellular adhesions at the luminal/apical surface in lung tissue.
source: Immunostaining for Zonula Occludens-1 (ZO-1), a marker of tight junctions, labeled intercellular adhesions at the luminal/apical surface (Figure 2D) as previously reported (Yang et al., 2016), suggesting that the epithelial branches form an intact cellular monolayer and display barrier function.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The epithelial branches form an intact cellular monolayer and display barrier function.
source: Immunostaining for Zonula Occludens-1 (ZO-1), a marker of tight junctions, labeled intercellular adhesions at the luminal/apical surface (Figure 2D) as previously reported (Yang et al., 2016), suggesting that the epithelial branches form an intact cellular monolayer and display barrier function.
evidence: This is an inference based on ZO-1 staining pattern.

claim: Lysosome-Associated Membrane glycoProtein 3 (LAMP3) is a lysosomal marker localized to lamellar bodies in differentiated AT2 cells.
source: In addition, we found that Lysosome-Associated Membrane glycoProtein 3 (LAMP3), a lysosomal marker localized to lamellar bodies in differentiated AT2 cells (Chang et al., 2013; Desai et al., 2014), was localized in apical secretory organelles in SFTPC+ cells, indicating that these cells can differentiate into AT2 cells (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: LAMP3 was localized in apical secretory organelles in SFTPC+ cells.
source: In addition, we found that Lysosome-Associated Membrane glycoProtein 3 (LAMP3), a lysosomal marker localized to lamellar bodies in differentiated AT2 cells (Chang et al., 2013; Desai et al., 2014), was localized in apical secretory organelles in SFTPC+ cells, indicating that these cells can differentiate into AT2 cells (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a primary observation from immunostaining experiments, shown in Figure 2D.

claim: SFTPC+ cells can differentiate into AT2 cells.
source: In addition, we found that Lysosome-Associated Membrane glycoProtein 3 (LAMP3), a lysosomal marker localized to lamellar bodies in differentiated AT2 cells (Chang et al., 2013; Desai et al., 2014), was localized in apical secretory organelles in SFTPC+ cells, indicating that these cells can differentiate into AT2 cells (Figure 2D).

claim: Cultured alveolar progenitors differentiate morphologically and molecularly into AT1 and AT2 cells.
